questions.topic: Family of Circles & Radical Axis Properties
questions.category: Coordinate Geometry (Straight Lines & Circles) :: Advanced Mathematical Structure (Type 1)
questions.question:
In [Coordinate Geometry (Straight Lines & Circles)], find the equation of the radical axis of the two circles:
$S_1: x^2 + y^2 - 4x - 6y + 4 = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad S_2: x^2 + y^2 + 2x + 4y - 6 = 0$.
questions.solution: The equation of the radical axis is $S_1 - S_2 = 0 \implies (-4x - 2x) + (-6y - 4y) + (4 - (-6)) = 0 \implies -6x - 10y + 10 = 0 \implies 6x + 10y - 10 = 0$.
questions.explanation: Solve using rigorous mathematical proofs and transformations in Coordinate Geometry (Straight Lines & Circles).
tags: Family of Circles & Radical Axis Properties

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.topic: Family of Circles & Radical Axis Properties
questions.category: Coordinate Geometry (Straight Lines & Circles) :: Quantitative Deduction
questions.question:
Evaluate the integer value of the limit in [Coordinate Geometry (Straight Lines & Circles)]:
$$\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{x - \sin x}{x^3} \times 6$$
questions.solution: Using Taylor series $\sin x = x - \frac{x^3}{6} + O(x^5)$, we have $\frac{x - \sin x}{x^3} = \frac{1}{6} + O(x^2) \to \frac{1}{6}$. Multiplied by $6$, the value is $1$.
questions.explanation: Derive using rigorous mathematical theorems in Coordinate Geometry (Straight Lines & Circles).
tags: Family of Circles & Radical Axis Properties
